brief: Wooden silo built between 1913 and 1926: a 21-sided polygon 14 ft across inside, framed on 4x6 uprights and sheathed outside in horizontal 1x6 tongue-and-groove siding, with flat bands at each floor level, 26 ft to the eave. It carries a 21-sided conical roof of asphalt shingles on self-supporting rafters, about 31 ft to the peak, with a small gabled dormer; a column of hinged plank silo doors with steel ladder rungs runs up one side, and a gabled entry vestibule with a pair of board doors sits at the foot. Plank-roofed feed sheds join it on both sides. Measured drawings only, no photos. (Polygonal wood-sided silo; nearest vocabulary type is wood_stave.)
